title: The EC armor-line allowlist entry passes every EC private key: the leak scan and publish no longer flag a real EC key with its body
goal: The leak scan (kbcommon.leak_hits, which the tracked-file scan, check-trailers' neighbours and kbgit.py publish read) flags a private key armor block that carries key material for every armor kind, an EC one included, while the armor label quoted alone in prose (the secret-shapes article, the anchors ledger, commit 73331d8a6) still passes; the value-wide allowlist entry for the EC armor line is removed or replaced by an exception that cannot pass key material

run:
import base64, os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbcommon, kbpublic
allow = kbpublic.parse_allowlist(open("_tools/tests_allowlist.txt", encoding="utf-8").read())
dash = "-" * 5
body = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(96)).decode()
key = dash + "BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY" + dash + "\n" + body[:64] + "\n" + body[64:] + "\n" + dash + "END EC PRIVATE KEY" + dash + "\n"
label = "the armor line " + dash + "BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY" + dash + " names the format\n"
hit_key = bool(kbcommon.leak_hits(key, allow))
hit_label = bool(kbcommon.leak_hits(label, allow))
print("key with body flagged:", hit_key, "| bare label flagged:", hit_label)
sys.exit(0 if hit_key and not hit_label else 1)

notes: Found by the SP-tsb23kev review (reviewer session on origin/main 4125e63f4): BG-onc6wxd3's allowlist line 'secret -----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----' matches by value with no file or commit scope, and the SECRETS shape matches only the armor line, so any EC private key with its body passes leak_hits, the tracked-file scan and kbgit.py publish. Repro on 4125e63f4: 'key with body flagged: False | bare label flagged: False', exit 1. RSA and plain armor lines still hit. The fix is a critical guard (leak scan): one planted failure in test_leaks.py is allowed. Publishing stays the operator's.
